title: Chandi Devi Temple Haridwar | Complete Travel Guide with History & Ropeway Ride
content:
Chandi Devi Temple - Haridwar,

The Chandi Devi Temple is one of the most revered shrines in Haridwar, dedicated to Goddess Chandi, a powerful form of Goddess Parvati. Situated atop the Neel Parvat hill on the eastern bank of the Ganga River, this temple is not only a sacred pilgrimage site but also offers beautiful views of Haridwar city and the surrounding mountains.

The temple was originally built in the 8th century by the famous saint Adi Shankaracharya and later renovated in 1929 by King Suchat Singh of Kashmir. According to Hindu mythology, Goddess Chandi Devi rested here after slaying the demon kings Shumbh and Nishumbh. Because of this legend, the temple is considered a Shakti Peetha and holds great religious importance.

Reaching the temple itself is a unique experience. Pilgrims can either trek for about 3 km uphill through forested paths or take the Chandi Devi Ropeway (Udan Khatola), which offers a thrilling aerial ride with panoramic views of the Ganga and Haridwar below.

The temple attracts devotees throughout the year, especially during the Navratri festival and Chandi Chaudas, when thousands of pilgrims visit to seek blessings of the Goddess. Beyond its religious aura, Chandi Devi Temple is also loved by travelers for its natural setting, scenic beauty, and peaceful vibes.

Temple Timings:

Morning: 6:00 am – 12:00 pm

Evening: 3:00 pm – 6:00 pm
(Timings may vary during festivals, so plan accordingly)

How to Reach Chandi Devi Temple:

  • By Road: Haridwar is well connected from Delhi (5-6 hours by car). From Haridwar city, the base of the temple is around 4 km.
  • By Train: Haridwar Junction is the nearest railway station (4 km from the temple base).
  • By Air: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun is 35 km away.
  • Ropeway: The ropeway starts from the base and takes about 5–10 minutes to reach the temple.

Travel Tips: If visiting during Navratri, expect large crowds - arrive early, Ropeway tickets can sell out fast, so book early if possible, Wear comfortable footwear if you plan to trek uphill,Carry water, especially in summer months, Respect temple traditions and dress modestly.
excerpt: The Chandi Devi Temple Haridwar is a sacred Shakti Peetha located on Neel Parvat, known for its ropeway ride, temple trek, and Navratri celebrations. A must-visit for devotees, pilgrims, and tourists, it combines history, spirituality, and scenic views of Haridwar.

faqs.question: What is Chandi Devi Temple famous for?
faqs.answer: It is a Shakti Peetha dedicated to Goddess Chandi and is famous for legends of her victory over demons Shumbh and Nishumbh.

faqs.question: How to reach Chandi Devi Temple?
faqs.answer: You can trek 3 km uphill or take the ropeway (Udan Khatola) from Haridwar city.

faqs.question: Who built Chandi Devi Temple?
faqs.answer: The temple was established by Adi Shankaracharya in the 8th century and rebuilt by King Suchat Singh in 1929.

faqs.question: Which festival is celebrated at Chandi Devi Temple?
faqs.answer: Navratri and Chandi Chaudas are celebrated with great devotion.

faqs.answer: The temple base is about 4 km from Har Ki Pauri.
